info.title: wan/wan2.5-t2v-preview
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "wan/wan2.5-t2v-preview", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: This model's input has not been narrowed by Comfy yet. Router forwards the body to the partner unchanged, so the partner's own documentation is authoritative until a schema is authored for this model. Any JSON object is accepted here and by the server's pre-provider validation alike.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

code.description: Error code for a failed request, reported at the ROOT of the envelope rather than under `output` (not returned if the request succeeded).

message.description: Detailed information about a failed request, reported at the ROOT of the envelope rather than under `output` (not returned if the request succeeded). Read this before falling back to `output.message`.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Wan and HappyHorse models: the terminal `GET /proxy/wan/api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` document, forwarded unchanged. All three DashScope submit operations — `/api/v1/services/aigc/video-generation/video-synthesis` (video), `/api/v1/services/aigc/text2image/image-synthesis` (image) and `/api/v1/services/aigc/image2image/image-synthesis` (image) — are SUBMIT-AND-POLL (`routerresult/classification.go` records all three as `ReturnModeSubmitPoll` on the shared `wanTaskStatus` poll route), so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than the `{task_id, task_status}` handle the underlying submit answers with. That is the reading a modality-shaped guess gets backwards: unlike xAI and BytePlus, DashScope puts the IMAGE operations behind the same task queue as the video one, and all twenty ids answer this one document.
`output.task_status` is DashScope's own UPPERCASE vocabulary — `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, `UNKNOWN` — forwarded unchanged; `routerpollstate/families.go` `FamilyWan` treats `SUCCEEDED` as the one terminal success and the rest of the closed set as terminal failures.
WHICH LEAF CARRIES THE ASSET DEPENDS ON THE OPERATION, and a caller must select on the operation it submitted rather than on `output` being non-empty:
* VIDEO tasks (the eighteen video ids, submitted through
  `video-generation/video-synthesis`) put the generated video at
  `output.video_url`. An I2V task that also generated audio carries it separately at
  `output.check_audio`; that is not a substitute for `output.video_url`.
* IMAGE tasks (`wan/wan2.5-t2i-preview` through `text2image/image-synthesis` and
  `wan/wan2.5-i2i-preview` through `image2image/image-synthesis`) put each generated
  image at `output.results[].url`. `results` is a LIST — DashScope defaults to four
  images and honours `parameters.n` — and an individual element may carry `code` and
  `message` INSTEAD of `url` when that one image failed while the task as a whole
  succeeded, so a caller must read `url` per element rather than assume the list is
  uniform. `output.task_metrics` reports the TOTAL/SUCCEEDED/FAILED split for
  exactly that case.

A `SUCCEEDED` whose `output` carries neither leaf is a success that produced nothing, not a finished generation; through Router that distinction is already settled, because `routerpollstate` answers it as a Comfy Router error rather than with the provider document. A FAILED task reports its reason at `output.code`/`output.message`, and DashScope may additionally report a top-level `code`/`message` on the envelope itself; read the ROOT pair first and fall back to the nested one, which is the order the first-party Wan poller uses.
The URLs are DashScope-hosted and valid for 24 HOURS from completion, so download them promptly rather than storing them. `usage` reports DashScope's own generation accounting — its numbers, not the Comfy charge — and its fields are per-operation (`video_duration`/`video_ratio`/`video_count` for T2V, `duration`/`SR` for I2V and wan3.0-video, `size`/`image_count` for T2I).
SCHEMA VS EXAMPLE: the schema below is the ONE shared `WanTaskQueryResponse` all twenty ids answer with — the wan/* output components are split by modality only so that each published document carries an example of its OWN operation, never a video example printed under an image model. The split is presentational; the contract is not.
THIS DOCUMENT describes a TEXT-to-video id, so its example is the T2V shape: the asset at `output.video_url` and the `video_duration`/`video_ratio`/`video_count` usage triple. `duration`/`SR` are the conditioned-video spelling and are not what a T2V task reports.

output.actual_prompt: a single red maple leaf falling onto still water, slow motion, shallow depth of field
output.orig_prompt: a single red maple leaf falling onto still water

actual_prompt.description: Actual prompt after intelligent rewriting (for video tasks)

check_audio.description: Audio URL for I2V tasks with audio generation

code.description: The error code for the failed request (not returned if request is successful)

message.description: Detailed information about the failed request (not returned if request is successful)

results.description: List of task results for image generation tasks

actual_prompt.description: Actual prompt after intelligent rewriting (if enabled)

code.description: Image error code (returned when some tasks fail)

message.description: Image error information (returned when some tasks fail)

task_metrics.description: Task result statistics for image generation tasks

video_url.description: Video URL for completed video generation tasks. Link validity period 24 hours

usage.description: Output information statistics. Only successful results are counted

SR.description: Video resolution level (I2V and wan3.0-video tasks)

duration.description: Duration of generated video in seconds (I2V and wan3.0-video tasks)

fps.description: Frame rate of the generated video (wan3.0-video tasks)

input_video_duration.description: Duration of the input video in seconds, 0.0 when no video input (wan3.0-video tasks)

output_video_duration.description: Duration of the output video in seconds (wan3.0-video tasks)

ratio.description: Aspect ratio of the generated video, e.g. 16:9 (wan3.0-video tasks)

video_duration.description: Duration of generated video in seconds (T2V tasks)
